tips.runAc: Run the A/C for ten minutes every couple of weeks, even in winter — it keeps the compressor seals lubricated.
tips.recirculate: Use recirculation in traffic to keep exhaust fumes out, then switch back to fresh air to stop the windows misting.
tips.filter: A clogged cabin filter cuts airflow and makes the whole system work harder. It is the cheapest fix on this list.
tips.smell: A musty smell when you start the A/C usually means moisture in the evaporator. Running the fan without cooling for the last minute of a drive helps dry it.

faq.q1: How does AutoPilot know when a service is due?
faq.a1: Each reminder can be triggered by a date, by an odometer reading, or by whichever arrives first. When you update your odometer, distance-based reminders re-evaluate immediately.
faq.q2: Why does my fuel economy look wrong?
faq.a2: Economy is only calculated from full fill-ups, because a partial fill does not tell us how much fuel the previous distance actually used. Mark a fill-up as a full tank to include it.
faq.q3: Can I track more than one car?
faq.a3: Yes. Add as many vehicles as you like under Vehicle information, and switch between them from the home screen. Services, fuel and documents are kept separately per vehicle.
faq.q4: What happens when a document expires?
faq.a4: AutoPilot warns you 30 days ahead, then marks the document expired. The record stays so you keep the history.
faq.a5: Your records are tied to your account and are not shared. You can export everything or delete your account at any time from Privacy & security.
faq.a6: Yes. Due items always appear on the home screen and calendar. Notifications are the extra nudge, not the only one.

about.title: About AutoPilot
about.missionBody: Car maintenance goes wrong in the gap between knowing something is due and remembering it at the right moment. AutoPilot closes that gap: log it once, and the app tells you when it matters.
about.creditsBody: Built with Expo and React Native.

home.odometerBody: This is the number everything else is built on. Services, reminders and fuel economy are all measured against it.
home.updateBody: Tap here whenever you notice the reading has moved. Takes five seconds, and AutoPilot recalculates what is due.
home.quickActionsBody: Fill up, get a service done, or set a reminder — all from here, without digging through menus.
home.tabsBody: Maintenance history, your calendar, and the full set of tools under Services.

howItWorks.title: How AutoPilot works
howItWorks.subtitle: A two-minute walkthrough
howItWorks.replayTour: Show me on the app instead
howItWorks.mileageBody: Your odometer reading is what AutoPilot measures against. Keep it current and the app works out the rest on its own.
howItWorks.mileagePoint1: Update it from the home screen in about five seconds.
howItWorks.mileagePoint2: The app asks for it only when the reading has gone stale.
howItWorks.remindersBody: Service schedules are written as "10,000 km or 12 months", so reminders here work the same way.
howItWorks.remindersPoint1: Trigger by date, by distance, or whichever arrives first.
howItWorks.remindersPoint2: Repeating reminders roll forward when you mark them done.
howItWorks.fuelBody: Log a fill-up and AutoPilot works out your real-world consumption, then tells you when it shifts.
howItWorks.fuelPoint1: Only full fill-ups count, because a partial fill cannot tell you what the distance actually used.
howItWorks.fuelPoint2: Two fill-ups is enough to get your first figure.
howItWorks.documentsBody: Insurance, registration and your licence, stored with their expiry dates attached.
howItWorks.documentsPoint1: You get a warning 30 days before anything runs out.
howItWorks.documentsPoint2: Attach the file once and open or share it from anywhere.
howItWorks.toolsBody: Everything else sits under Services, ready when you need it.
howItWorks.toolsPoint1: Look up a dashboard fault code and see whether it is safe to drive.
howItWorks.toolsPoint2: Plan a trip and get the fuel cost from your own economy figure.
